texts: mixed: the rule has the right shape and fires, but written with a bare "When" it lost the link tying each redistribution to the convening it happens during, so you cannot ask which sitting a given redistribution belonged to. Use the explicit recurrence wording, which produced the complete rule in your next sentence: "Whenever the Council convenes, the Council redistributes mire-essence across the lantern-stations."
good. a fireable per-occasion rule carrying the Council, the essence and the stations, with each reallocation tied to the meeting it happens during.
good. the restriction "productive" becomes part of the rule's condition rather than a new kind of station, and the contribution to the central pool is fully covered.
good. mirrors the previous sentence — a fireable rule restricted to burdened stations, with the central pool recorded as the source of what is drawn.

bad: capitalizing the plural "Keepers" makes the translator read it as the proper name of a body, and each available reading then loses half the content — a name with nothing said about who they are, or (as here) a group of keepers with the name dropped. If "keepers" is their role rather than a title, lower-case it: "The keepers record the redistribution in the Watch ledgers."
